title: Codimension-one Cartier part of a subscheme on a regular surface
statement: Let $X$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$, and let $Z\subsetneq X$ be a closed subscheme with ideal $\mathcal I_Z$. There exist an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ such that $\mathcal I_Z=\mathcal L\mathcal J$, and $T=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J)$ is a finite set of closed points of codimension $2$ contained in $|Z|$. Here codimension of a point is the dimension of its local ring. The empty set $T$ and the unit ideal $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X$ are allowed. Conventions: [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Tag 0AGB (divisors-lemma-codim-1-part), regular-scheme case, with the factorization by the invertible divisor ideal in resolve.tex, Tag 0BIB (resolve-lemma-turn-into-effective-Cartier), proof first paragraph.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_Z$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], on an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is $\widetilde{I_U}$; $I_U$ is finitely generated by Noetherianity. Since $X$ is integral and $Z\ne X$, the generic point $\eta$ is outside $|Z|$: otherwise every element of $I_U$ maps to zero in the fraction field of the domain $A$, hence $I_U=0$ on every nonempty affine, giving $Z=X$. The space $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]; its closed subspace $|Z|$ is Noetherian, since its closed subsets are closed in $X$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components, lem-sc-scheme-sober], $|Z|$ has finitely many irreducible components, each with a unique generic point. Keep those generic points $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_r$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}=1$. Give their closures the reduced induced structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. These are integral closed subschemes $D_i$, since they are reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0AGB, proof first and last paragraphs: the codimension-one components

proof.text: By [lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations], each $\mathcal P_i=\mathcal I_{D_i}$ is an effective Cartier ideal and $R_i=\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}$ is a DVR. The ideal $\mathcal I_{\xi_i}$ is nonzero: in an affine domain the ideal of $Z$ is nonzero and localization is injective. It is proper because $\xi_i\in |Z|$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] choose a generator $b_i\ne0$ of this ideal and a uniformizer $t_i$ of $R_i$. The DVR is Noetherian, as a local ring of the regular scheme, so [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] writes $b_i=u_it_i^{a_i}$ for a unit $u_i$ and $a_i\ge0$. Thus $\mathcal I_{\xi_i}=(t_i^{a_i})$, and $a_i>0$ since this ideal is proper. Replacing a uniformizer by a unit multiple leaves its power ideal unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, proof first paragraph: the exponents at the generic DVRs

proof.text: Define $\mathcal L=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal P_i^{a_i}$, with empty product $\mathcal O_X$. This is a quasi-coherent ideal: on an affine trivializing the finitely many factors, its sections form the product of the corresponding principal ideals, and these products commute with restriction to principal affine opens. By [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], each factor has a local nonzerodivisor generator; their product $f=\prod_i f_i^{a_i}$ is again a nonzerodivisor, because multiplication by it is a composite of injective multiplication maps. Thus $\mathcal L$ is an effective Cartier ideal.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, construction D=sum a_i D_i; Tag 01WT (divisors-definition-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors) and Tag 01WU (divisors-lemma-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors), local product calculation

proof.text: We show $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal L$ on stalks. Fix $x$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, a domain. Discard the $D_i$ not containing $x$, whose ideals have unit stalk. By [lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations], the remaining $f_i$ are prime and $\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}=A_{(f_i)}$. They are pairwise nonassociate: distinct prime divisors through $x$ have distinct generic points, hence distinct corresponding prime ideals of $A$. For $h\in\mathcal I_x$, Step 2 gives $h/1\in f_i^{a_i}A_{(f_i)}$. Clearing its one denominator gives $s h=f_i^{a_i}b$ with $s\notin(f_i)$; the equality holds in $A$ since $A$ is a domain. Induction on $a_i$ using primeness gives $f_i^{a_i}\mid h$: first $f_i\mid h$, then cancel one $f_i$ and repeat. If $h=f_1^{a_1}h_1$, primeness and nonassociation imply that every $f_j^{a_j}$ with $j>1$ still divides $h_1$, by cancelling the $f_1$ factors one at a time. Inducting on the finite list gives $\prod_i f_i^{a_i}\mid h$. Hence $\mathcal I_x\subseteq\mathcal L_x$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, middle paragraphs: contraction from A_(f_i) and successive prime-power division

proof.text: Define the ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ intrinsically by $\mathcal J(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):a\mathcal L|_V\subseteq\mathcal I|_V\}$. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ where $\mathcal L=(f)$, Step 4 gives $I_U\subseteq fA$. Multiplication by the nonzerodivisor $f$ is an isomorphism $A\to fA$, so its inverse image $J_U=\{a\in A:fa\in I_U\}$ satisfies $I_U=fJ_U$. If $I_U=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, uniquely write $h_j=fg_j$; cancellation shows $J_U=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$. This description commutes with localization: a localized element $a/s$ has $fa/s\in (I_U)_s$ exactly when a power of $s$ multiplies $fa$ into $I_U$. Thus $\mathcal J|_U=\widetilde{J_U}$, and the intrinsic definition makes these local ideals agree on overlaps, even when the equation $f$ changes by a unit. This proves that $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and that $\mathcal I=\mathcal L\mathcal J$ [pqf-def-coherent, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 0BIB (resolve-lemma-turn-into-effective-Cartier), proof first paragraph: division by the invertible divisor ideal

proof.text:
The residual ideal is the unit ideal at every point of codimension at most one. First it is the unit ideal at $\eta$, where both $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal L$ are the unit ideal. This is the only codimension-zero point: any other point has the strict generalization $\eta$ and therefore has local dimension at least one by the cited chain formula. If a codimension-one point $y$ belongs to $|Z|$, a generic point $\xi$ of a component of $|Z|$ containing $y$ generalizes $y$. Since $\eta
otin |Z|$, $\xi
e\eta$; if $\xi
e y$, the chain $y,\xi,\eta$ contradicts the dimension-one hypothesis by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]. Thus $y=\xi_i$ for some $i$. At $\xi_i$ the other divisor ideals are units, since two distinct codimension-one component generic points cannot specialize to one another. Step 2 therefore gives $\mathcal I_{\xi_i}=\mathcal L_{\xi_i}$, so the local division of Step 5 gives $\mathcal J_{\xi_i}=\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}$. At any $x
otin |Z|$, $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$; the inclusion $\mathcal I_x\subseteq\mathcal L_x$ forces $\mathcal L_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and the product equality forces $\mathcal J_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. This also shows $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J)\subseteq |Z|$.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, conclusion: equality at codimension-one points; Tag 0BIB, residual support

proof.text: The quotient $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent of finite type: on the affines of Step 5 it is $\widetilde{A/J_U}$, generated by $1$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] says its support $T$ is closed. Step 6 excludes codimensions zero and one. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], each local dimension is the supremum of lengths of generalization chains and is at most $\dim X=2$, so every $t\in T$ has codimension exactly $2$. A strict specialization $t\leadsto t'$ would extend a length-two chain ending at $t$ to a length-three chain in $X$, contradicting $\dim X=2$. Thus each $t$ is closed in $X$. The closed subspace $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Each has a generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; that point is closed in $X$, so its closure is a singleton. The finitely many components therefore make $T$ a finite set of closed points of codimension $2$. The argument includes $T=\varnothing$ and $r=0$, giving the allowed unit ideal $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X$.
